reviews.body: Thanks. The baseline read now goes through `matchOnce`, so an old SDK gets the same retry as the verdict. The negative test for another refusal is good, and the suppression record got smaller. The merge queue runs the benchmark for this path.

comments.body: Thanks for your first pull request to Reticle! A maintainer aims to review within two days. Before then, `pnpm verify` locally catches most of what CI will, and [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/reticlehq/reticle/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) explains the rest. If CI does not start, a maintainer needs to approve it for first-time contributors; that is normal.

Thanks, this is the fix #2065 asked for, and reusing `matchOnce` is right. CI fails on `engine` lint (`pnpm lint` exits 2). Since the PR touches `baseline.ts` and `predicate-element.ts`, AGENTS.md rule 17 applies: brace every `if` in a changed file and prune its suppressions. Run `npx eslint --fix engine/src/evidence/baseline.ts engine/src/question/predicate/predicate-element.ts`, then `npx eslint src --prune-suppressions` in `engine`, then `pnpm verify`. The yoda rule (`undefined === x`) is the other common one here.
